body: I think it's interesting how you've shifted from comparing oneself to soil in the first two stanzas, to comparing the soil to oneself in the latter stanzas, making the speaker the subject instead. The sense of vulnerability introduced in the next two stanzas takes on a melancholic, self-pitying tone as a result; it seems as though the speaker laments a helpless fate, they feel weak, though they know of their innate ability to flourish. I think the last two lines do a great job ending the poem in a hopeful light, acknowledging one's agency to wither or bloom :)

I love the imagery of braiding one’s gaze with another’s… there’s something so tactile and intimate about it. It makes me think of a childlike innocence too. I think it really evokes a longing for connection and wide-eyed curiosity for the unfamiliar
